chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three [types of women] may marry at any time [without waiting for a waiting period]: the one who has not yet menstruated, and her like who does not menstruate.' I asked: 'What is her limit/definition?' He said: 'When she is less than nine years old.' And the one who has not been entered into (consummated), and the one who has despaired of menstruation, and her like who does not menstruate.' I asked: 'What is her limit/definition?' He said: 'When she is fifty years old.'

key_terms.يَتَزَوَّجْنَ: They may marry (implying no waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of women exempt from the Islamic waiting period (Iddah)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the legal criteria for women exempt from the waiting period ('iddah) due to the absence of menstruation, specifically defining pre-pubescent girls as under nine years old and menopausal women as over fifty. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'iddah is intrinsically linked to the menstrual cycle, distinguishing these categories from those who have been consummated but are merely barren or pre-menopausal. The specific age markers provide a clear temporal boundary for applying the exemption in cases of divorce or widowhood.
